questions.def: Use 'an' before a noun starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: My brother, ___ engineer, works in London.

questions.def: Use 'the' before superlatives to specify a unique member.
questions.question: Shakespeare, ___ most famous playwright, wrote many sonnets.

questions.def: Use the correct article and past participle for passive meaning.
questions.question: My professor, ___ expert in the field, gave a lecture.

questions.def: Use 'the' with unique nouns and definite appositives.
questions.question: Paris, ___ capital of France, is a beautiful city.

questions.def: Use 'a' before a noun to introduce it generally.
questions.question: My dog, ___ golden retriever, loves to play fetch.

questions.def: Use the past participle 'called' for a passive appositive.
questions.question: My neighbor, ___ Mr. Smith, is very friendly.

questions.def: Use 'an' before a word starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: My car, ___ old Ford, needs repairs.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'genius' to describe a type of person.
questions.question: Einstein, ___ genius, revolutionized physics.

questions.def: Use passive voice; 'elected' describes her state.
questions.question: She was ___ president of the club.

questions.def: Use 'the' with superlative adjectives to denote uniqueness.
questions.question: Mount Everest, ___ highest peak, attracts many climbers.

questions.def: Use 'a' to introduce the appositive describing the apartment.
questions.question: My apartment, ___ small studio, is near the park.

questions.def: 'Named' is a passive appositive, specifying the book title.
questions.question: The book, ___ 'The Secret Garden,' is a classic.

questions.def: Use 'a' before a consonant sound to introduce a profession.
questions.question: My aunt, ___ doctor, works at the local hospital.

questions.def: Use 'an' before a word starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: My colleague, ___ experienced programmer, helped me debug the code.

questions.def: Use 'considered' as a passive appositive describing the boss.
questions.question: My boss, ___ a fair leader, is respected by all.

questions.def: Use 'the' before superlatives to show a unique entity.
questions.question: The Amazon, ___ longest river, flows through South America.

questions.def: Use 'a' to introduce the appositive describing the phone.
questions.question: My phone, ___ new iPhone, has a great camera.

questions.def: Use 'appointed' as a passive form to describe his role.
questions.question: He was ___ chairman of the board.

questions.def: Use 'a' to introduce the appositive describing his occupation.
questions.question: My neighbor's son, ___ student, is studying abroad.

questions.def: Use 'a' to describe the appositive describing his profession.
questions.question: My uncle, ___ retired teacher, enjoys traveling.

questions.def: 'That's' is incorrect. 'Who is' or 'who' is more appropriate.
questions.question: My friend, that's a programmer, works at Google now.

questions.def: 'Found' is the past participle and correct passive appositive.
questions.question: The treasure, ___ hidden for years, was recovered.

questions.def: Use 'an' before a word starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: My favorite movie, ___ action film, is 'The Matrix'.

questions.def: Use 'the' because it is the definite capital city.
questions.question: He visited Rome, ___ capital city, last summer.

questions.def: Use 'a' before a noun in apposition that introduces a new, non-specific role.
questions.question: My friend, ___ doctor, is very busy.

questions.def: Use 'the' when the appositive is unique or specifically identified.
questions.question: Professor Smith, ___ head of department, gave a lecture.

questions.def: Appositive requires an article before the noun 'expert'.
questions.question: She consulted Dr. Jones, ___ in the field.

questions.def: Use 'a' when the appositive describes a general quality.
questions.question: The CEO, ___ woman with vision, inspired the team.

questions.def: 'A' is used because 'small village' is non-defining appositive.
questions.question: My hometown, ___ small village, is quiet.

questions.def: 'A' should be used before 'great success' because it is non-specific.
questions.question: His novel, the great success, surprised everyone.
